newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: BCP official held on fraud suspicion.
newsitem.headline: BCP official held on fraud suspicion.

text.p: A senior official of Portugal's biggest private bank Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP) has been held in a Lisbon jail for more than a week suspected of having committed fraud, a bank spokesman said on Tuesday.

Jose Pinto Bastos confirmed a report in Publico newspaper on Monday which reported that Jose Dias Silva, a senior official in BCP's private banking division, was held on suspicion of having committed fraud 11 years ago when he worked for Banco Portugues do Atlantico (BPA). BCP bought BPA in March last year.

Publico said Dias Silva was accused of having offered favours to a client of BPA, businessman Alambre dos Santos. Dos Santos was briefly detained and later released after securing bail, the newspaper said.
Dias Silva was waiting for a judge to set bail terms, Pinto Bastos said. It was not known when Dias Silva would face trial.
Pinto Bastos told Reuters that BCP would stand by Dias Silva who would return to his duties at the bank when he wins bail.
"The board has complete confidence in Dias Silva," he said.
BCP shares stood at 1,877 escudos, down eight, on Lisbon bourse on Tuesday morning.
